title: `torch.compile` silent bug in GGUF dequant, possibly because of `view(dtype)`

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

I caught this bug when implementing GGUF dequant in torch. I've started related discussions at https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF/issues/405 and https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/40070 . I've tried my best to make a minimal reproducer:
```python
import torch

def generate_blocks_bf16(n_blocks):
    data = torch.zeros((n_blocks, 2), dtype=torch.uint8)
    data[:, 0] = 0x80
    data[:, 1] = 0x3F
    return data

def generate_blocks_Q6_K(n_blocks):
    data = torch.zeros((n_blocks, 210), dtype=torch.uint8)
    data[:, 192:208] = 1
    data[:, 208] = 0x00
    data[:, 209] = 0x3C
    return data

def dequantize_blocks_BF16(blocks, dtype):
    return (blocks.view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32) << 16).view(torch.float32)

def split_block_dims(blocks, *args):
    n_max = blocks.shape[1]
    dims = list(args) + [n_max - sum(args)]
    xs = torch.split(blocks, dims, dim=1)
    return xs

def view_float16(x):
    return x.view(torch.float16)

def dequantize_blocks_Q6_K(blocks, dtype):
    QK_K = 256
    (ql, qh, scales, d) = split_block_dims(blocks, QK_K // 2, QK_K // 4, QK_K // 16)

    scales = scales.view(torch.int8).to(dtype)
    d = view_float16(d).to(dtype)
    d = d * scales

    n_blocks = blocks.shape[0]
    ql = ql.reshape((n_blocks, -1, 1, 64))

    return d

def wrap_compile(func):
    @torch.compile
    def _func(blocks, dtype):
        return func(blocks, dtype)

    return _func

dequantize_blocks_BF16_compiled = wrap_compile(dequantize_blocks_BF16)
dequantize_blocks_Q6_K_compiled = wrap_compile(dequantize_blocks_Q6_K)

device = "cpu"
n_blocks = 32

blocks_bf16 = generate_blocks_bf16(n_blocks).to(device)
blocks_Q6_K = generate_blocks_Q6_K(n_blocks).to(device)

out_bf16 = dequantize_blocks_BF16(blocks_bf16, torch.float32)
print("BF16 mean", out_bf16.mean().item())

out_Q6_K = dequantize_blocks_Q6_K(blocks_Q6_K, torch.float32)
print("Q6_K mean", out_Q6_K.mean().item())

out_bf16_compiled = dequantize_blocks_BF16_compiled(blocks_bf16, torch.float32)
print("BF16 mean compiled", out_bf16_compiled.mean().item())

out_Q6_K_compiled = dequantize_blocks_Q6_K_compiled(blocks_Q6_K, torch.float32)
print("Q6_K mean compiled", out_Q6_K_compiled.mean().item())
```
To pass the test, "Q6_K mean" should be the same as "Q6_K mean compiled". When the test fails, the output is like
```
BF16 mean 1.0
Q6_K mean 1.0
BF16 mean compiled 1.0
Q6_K mean compiled 0.0625
``` 
It fails on both CPU and CUDA.

Interestingly, if I comment out `out_bf16_compiled = dequantize_blocks_BF16_compiled(blocks_bf16, torch.float32)`, then the test passes.

Although `ql = ql.reshape((n_blocks, -1, 1, 64))` does not affect `d`, if I comment out it, the test passes.

I guess there is some undefined behavior like out-of-bounds memory access when we call `view(dtype)` and the number of bytes of the element changes.

Log with `TORCH_TRACE`: [dedicated_log_torch_trace_gox8spt4.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24696736/dedicated_log_torch_trace_gox8spt4.log)

### Error logs

No error. It silently gives wrong numbers or nan.
